paper.title: SkillMOO: Multi-Objective Optimization of Agent Skills for Software Engineering
paper.central_claim: SE agent skill bundles should be treated as multi-objective search objects; SkillMOO evolves bundles via LLM-proposed edits (pruning, substitution, reordering, rewriting) and NSGA-II Pareto selection on pass rate and inference cost, achieving the top pass-rate rank on 11 of 12 non-zero-pass SkillsBench SE tasks with cost reductions up to 32.1% over static bundles and pass-rate gains up to 42 percentage points, and pruning/substitution dominate successful edits.
paper.claim_scope: 16 SkillsBench SE tasks (4 with zero pass for all methods), GLM-5 as solver and optimizer, population 4 x 3 generations, 10 runs per method per task, LLM-expanded 40-43-test verifiers.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref unavailable to the worker subagent at write time; model_type recorded per controller dispatch instruction (agent_model=haiku slot -> claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]).

materials.notes: HTML-converted text v3 (ASE 2026 NIER); Figure 1 image not viewable, caption read. The SkillOptimizer prompts and replication package are referenced externally and not in the text.

evidence.quote: current practice treats them as static, hand-crafted assets, or evolved on pass rate alone.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: static or pass-rate-only skills.

evidence.quote: a skill can improve task success while substantially raising token cost, or introducing misleading guidance.
evidence.support_explanation: Stated trade-off motivating a two-objective formulation.

evidence.quote: many public SWE skills provide no pass rate improvement
evidence.support_explanation: Cited external evidence (SWE-Skills-Bench) that skills can fail to help and add token overhead.

evidence.quote: demonstrate that skills can themselves be optimized through iterative refinement, but they focus on pass rate alone.
evidence.support_explanation: Closest neighbors (EvoSkill, Meta Context Engineering, EvoSkills) optimize pass rate only; cost-aware selection is the stated delta.

evidence.quote: SkillMOO treats a skill bundle as a candidate solution, evaluates it with a task solver agent, and uses a skill optimizer agent to propose edits such as pruning, substitution, reordering, and rewriting.
evidence.support_explanation: Operation: solver-optimizer loop over skill bundles.

evidence.quote: Generation 0 seeds the population with candidates sampled as diverse subsets of the available skill pool.
evidence.support_explanation: Initial population = subsets of existing skills.

evidence.quote: The skill optimizer agent receives each surviving bundle together with its evaluation evidence and decides what change is most likely to improve the pass/cost tradeoff
evidence.support_explanation: Proposer sees evaluation evidence (pass, cost, runtime, failure traces).

evidence.quote: non-dominated sorting and crowding-distance tie-breaking on the two objectives below; the top-ranked survivors breed the next generation’s population.
evidence.support_explanation: Selection: standard NSGA-II on (pass rate, cost).

evidence.quote: Each method is run 10 times per task; a run passes only when its solution passes the full automated test suite, so pass rate is the fraction of passing runs.
evidence.support_explanation: 10 runs per method per task; binary pass per run.

evidence.quote: we expanded every suite to 40–43 tests with GPT-5.4
evidence.support_explanation: Verifier expanded by an LLM from 3-10 tests to 40-43.

evidence.quote: Each added test was checked manually against the task specification and reference environment, generated without skill content, and applied uniformly across methods.
evidence.support_explanation: Mitigation for LLM-generated tests.

evidence.quote: The evaluation uses population size 4 and 3 generations, which are chosen to bound optimization budget
evidence.support_explanation: Search budget: population 4, 3 generations.

evidence.quote: with per-candidate evaluation costs of $0.1–$14
evidence.support_explanation: Per-candidate cost range (full sentence continues: 900 s timeout, $1-$15 per-task overhead).

evidence.quote: they were produced by the same model family used for task solving, which may introduce shared reasoning biases in borderline cases
evidence.support_explanation: Author-acknowledged threat on test generation (note: the text elsewhere says GPT-5.4 generated tests and GLM-5 solves).

evidence.quote: We evaluate SkillMOO , ori_skill (original skill bundle), and no_skill (no guidance)
evidence.support_explanation: Only two baselines: static original bundle and no skills; no pass-only search, random search or equal-budget alternative.
Averages: SkillMOO pass 0.39 / cost 0.71; ori_skill 0.14 / 0.89; no_skill 0.21 / 0.64. Static original skills average lower pass than no skills.

evidence.quote: SkillMOO achieves the top pass rate rank on 11 of 12 non-zero-pass tasks
evidence.support_explanation: Headline result.

evidence.quote: 4 tasks yield zero pass for all methods
evidence.support_explanation: Four tasks have zero pass for all methods and are excluded from comparison (failure denominator disclosed).

evidence.quote: the strongest gain on a non-trivial task is on Task 5 : pass rate rises from 0.16 to 0.37 (+21.3 percentage points) while cost falls by 32.1% and runtime by 23.6%
evidence.support_explanation: Best cost-reduction example.

evidence.quote: with pass rate gains up to 42 percentage points
evidence.support_explanation: Abstract figure that does not match Table 2 differences versus ori_skill (e.g. Task 1: 0.90 vs 0.10).
Task 1 has a single-skill bundle: SkillMOO 0.90 pass vs ori_skill 0.10 and no_skill 0.60, so gains here cannot come from pruning and must come from content edits/reordering.

evidence.quote: optimization costs range from $1.76 to $13.73.
evidence.support_explanation: Per-task search overhead.

evidence.quote: approximate cost-only break-even of 5–682 reuses (median 45)
evidence.support_explanation: Reuse needed to recover search cost; assumes the optimized bundle is reused on the same task.

evidence.quote: Because the edits are filtered from search traces, RQ3 should be read as exploratory pattern evidence rather than an independent causal study.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors disclaim causal reading of the edit-pattern analysis.

evidence.quote: Add Skills shows 0/9 pass improvements across its three sub-types
evidence.support_explanation: Descriptive edit statistics over a filtered archive.

evidence.quote: First, our evaluation covers a single benchmark, with 1–8 initial skills
evidence.support_explanation: Scope threat: single benchmark; one LLM (GLM-5).

evidence.quote: is an open empirical question
evidence.support_explanation: Transfer to other coding agents is untested (continuation: "whether the MOO framing and Pareto improvements transfer ... is an open empirical question").

evidence.quote: Future work should isolate edit operations through controlled ablations, randomized edit proposals, and repeated validation
evidence.support_explanation: Authors state controlled ablations and randomized edits are future work.

evidence.quote: with Scott-Knott ESD confirming statistical significance.
evidence.support_explanation: Statistical ranking via Scott-Knott ESD over 10-run vectors.

evidence.quote: fractional values arise from run-to-run variation in the selected candidate
evidence.support_explanation: Each of the 10 SkillMOO runs performs its own search and selects its own candidate (so a run result is the outcome of a search); whether the reported pass is a fresh re-execution is not stated.

evidence.quote: each one-percent HV gain costs well under two U.S. cents in search fees
evidence.support_explanation: Cost-per-HV efficiency statement.

evidence.quote: the Pareto archive retains alternatives for a deployment budget or reliability target rather than simply choosing the highest-pass run.
evidence.support_explanation: Final-selection rule from the archive is not specified beyond this remark.

evidence.quote: RQ3 uses only edits drawn from the Pareto archive of fully evaluated candidates
evidence.support_explanation: Edit analysis restricted to archive members with non-zero deltas (selection-filtered).

evidence.quote: Each child is then evaluated by the same task solver.
evidence.support_explanation: Children evaluated by the same solver and verifier used for selection.

evidence.quote: Notably, no_skill achieves rank 1 cost on 12 of 16 tasks and has the lowest mean cost on every task
evidence.support_explanation: No-skill is cheapest on every task; SkillMOO is not cost-dominant.

signatures.object: Per-task skill bundle (subset and edited versions of the task SkillsBench skill pool: instructions, scripts, resources).
signatures.information: Per-candidate evaluation evidence: pass rate, cost, runtime, failure traces from the full verifier test suite (40-43 tests).
signatures.operation: Population 4, 3 generations. Optimizer agent (GLM-5) proposes remove/replace/add/reorder/rewrite edits per surviving bundle; solver agent (GLM-5) evaluates each child; NSGA-II ranks by (-pass, cost) with crowding distance and survivors breed the next generation.
signatures.output: Pareto archive of evaluated bundles; one bundle selected per run (selection rule from the archive not specified).
signatures.conditions: Per-candidate timeout 900 s; per-task budget about $1-$15 and under three hours.
signatures.feedback: Verifier pass/fail (oracle test suite for the same task) and measured USD cost/runtime.
signatures.selection_rule: NSGA-II non-dominated sorting on pass rate and cost.
signatures.selection_data: The same task and same verifier test suite used later to report results; candidates evaluated by the same solver.
signatures.persistence: Task-specific optimized bundle / Pareto archive that can be reused on the same task; routing/reuse across tasks is future work.
signatures.later_use: Reuse on repeated runs of the same task (break-even 5-682 reuses).
signatures.claimed_effect: Top pass-rate rank 11/12; Task 5 pass 0.16->0.37, cost -32.1%; average pass 0.39 vs 0.14 (ori_skill) and 0.21 (no_skill).
signatures.failure_boundary: Four tasks zero pass for all methods; no cross-task or cross-model transfer; edit analysis exploratory only; Add-skill edits never improved pass rate in the archive.

gap.author_gap: Agent skills are deployed as static hand-crafted assets or evolved on pass rate alone, although a skill can raise token cost or add misleading guidance, so pass rate and cost trade off.
gap.checked_gap: The trade-off is supported by cited external evidence (SkillsBench, SWE-Skills-Bench) and by the paper own Table 2, where the original bundles average lower pass (0.14) than no skills (0.21) and cost more than no skills. Pass-rate-only neighbors (EvoSkill, Meta Context Engineering, EvoSkills, ACE, GEPA, Meta-Harness) are named but not run; LLM-guided genetic improvement is the closest search precedent. The checked residue is narrow: cost-aware Pareto selection and pruning-dominant edits.
gap.lineage: Static curated skills (SkillsBench/SWE-Skills-Bench) -> pass-rate skill evolution (EvoSkill, EvoSkills) and context/prompt/harness optimizers (ACE, GEPA, Meta-Harness) -> LLM-guided GI with NSGA-II -> SkillMOO (cost-aware Pareto selection of skill bundles).
closest_adjacent: EvoSkill / EvoSkills / Meta Context Engineering: pass-rate-only skill evolution (E04)
LLM-guided Genetic Improvement: LLM edits + search-based software evolution (cited)
gap.residue: Skill bundles that raise cost or distract the agent; pass-only evolution ignores this.
gap.stakes: Up to 32.1% lower cost and 23.6% lower runtime with higher pass on the best task; typical search overhead $1.76-$13.73 per task.
gap.method_response: Treat bundle as a candidate in a bi-objective search; LLM edits informed by evaluation evidence; NSGA-II survivor selection.
gap.remaining_gap: No pass-only or budget-matched alternative search; cross-task/model transfer open; per-task optimization on the same verifier; mechanism of gains only descriptive.
unresolved: Whether cost-aware selection or LLM edits are needed relative to simple subset search at equal evaluation budget.
Whether reported SkillMOO pass rates are fresh re-evaluations or search-time outcomes.

tactic_steps_checked: Recast skill-bundle design as a bi-objective search/selection problem (pass, cost): executed
Solve with the mature machinery of the new object (NSGA-II, Pareto fronts, hypervolume, Scott-Knott ESD): executed
Independent faithfulness validation back to the original problem (does the optimized bundle help on unseen tasks/models): not executed
Boundary of the reframe stated: partial (single benchmark, one LLM)
success_checks: Chosen object unlocks machinery the native formulation lacked (cost-aware Pareto reasoning): partial
Reframe deletes a component instead of wrapping machinery around the old pipeline: unmet (adds an optimizer agent and NSGA-II around the existing skill pipeline)
failure_checks: Mechanical wrapper re-applying an existing solver to a new domain: partly applies (NSGA-II is off the shelf; new part is the cost objective)
Correspondence asserted not proven: applies, no argument that Pareto selection on training-time outcomes corresponds to deployment value
matches.reason: The operation is recasting skill engineering as multi-objective subset/edit selection solved with NSGA-II. C00/C21/C27 (transparency measurement, RL-as-supervised, game/equilibrium) do not describe it, so sub_id is null.

rs_pattern.reason: Main-card definition (recast as an optimization program so existing solvers apply) matches; no child card fits.
rs_pattern.resolves_problem: partial - Pareto-superior bundles are found per task against two static baselines, but whether the multi-objective reframing (versus pass-only or random search) caused it is not shown.

matches.reason: Population of skill bundles, LLM mutation grounded in evaluation evidence, executable verifier fitness, and selection by a Pareto frontier (NSGA-II) over pass rate and cost.

unassigned: Per-task, test-suite-conditioned specialization of a skill bundle (teaching-to-the-verifier) has no explicit condition in H16.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: RS: recast the problem as a well-studied optimization object (bi-objective selection) and apply its solvers. Domain: LLM-mutated population with executable fitness and Pareto selection. Both describe NSGA-II over skill bundles; the RS card emphasizes the reframing, the domain card the search loop and archive.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_and_differences: RS needs an independently validated faithfulness back to the original problem; the domain H16 needs an evaluator that is hard to game and a named axis of complementarity. The paper provides the axis (pass vs cost) but validates faithfulness only on the same verifier.

expectations.applies_when: An off-the-shelf solver is applied to a new object.
expectations.question: Does the reframe contribute new identifying structure beyond re-applying existing machinery?
expectations.reason: The new element is the cost objective and bundle edit operators; NSGA-II, hypervolume and Scott-Knott are off-the-shelf.

expectations.applies_when: Downstream metric gains are used as the validity argument.
expectations.question: Is faithfulness to the original problem validated by an oracle/causal intervention rather than only downstream gains?
expectations.reason: Edit-level causality is explicitly deferred; no fresh-task, fresh-model or randomized-edit check that Pareto-selected bundles are better for the original goal.

expectations.question: Is the solver scalability and assumption set examined?
expectations.reason: Per-task budget and overhead are reported and the search is small (4 x 3); larger skill pools and repositories are acknowledged as costlier but not tested.

expectations.question: Does the paper deliver an actionable principle rather than a descriptive observation?
expectations.reason: Prune/replace-over-add is offered as a principle but is drawn from filtered search traces and labeled exploratory.

expectations.question: Does the contribution live at the search level (what fitness measures or how evaluations are spent) rather than only the domain?
expectations.reason: Fitness is made two-objective with cost; this is the stated contribution.

expectations.applies_when: Selection pressure comes from an automatic evaluator.
expectations.question: Is the evaluator built before the loop and hard to game?
expectations.reason: Execution-based verifier with 40-43 tests and preserved build gates, but tests were LLM-expanded, are the same ones driving selection, and the optimizer sees failure traces from them; pass improvements arise when edits target verifier failures.

expectations.applies_when: Mutations are proposed by an LLM.
expectations.question: Are mutations grounded in what the evaluator observed?
expectations.reason: Optimizer receives each bundle with its evaluation evidence.

expectations.question: Does the frontier name the complementarity axis and earn its place by measured effect?
expectations.reason: Axis (pass vs cost) is named and hypervolume measured, but the final bundle choice from the archive and the benefit of keeping alternatives are not evaluated.

expectations.applies_when: A generic loop is pointed at a new domain.
expectations.question: Is there search-level novelty beyond a generic LLM-mutation + standard metaheuristic loop on skills?
expectations.reason: Cost-aware selection is search-level but NSGA-II, population and mutation loop are standard; no comparison shows it matters.

expectations.applies_when: A search method is compared with a single-evaluation static baseline.
expectations.question: Is there an equal-evaluation-budget alternative (random subset/edit search or pass-only evolution)?
expectations.reason: Only ori_skill and no_skill are run; SkillMOO consumes a multi-candidate search budget that baselines do not get.

expectations.applies_when: Reported per-run outcomes come from a stochastic search that selects among stochastic evaluations.
expectations.question: Is the selected bundle re-evaluated on fresh executions (or held-out tasks/tests) before reporting?
expectations.reason: The paper says each run selects its own candidate but does not say the final pass rate is a fresh re-execution; the same verifier is used for search and reporting.

expectations.applies_when: Headline numbers are stated in the abstract.
expectations.question: Do abstract effect sizes match Table 2?
expectations.reason: Abstract says gains up to 42 pp, yet Table 2 differences versus ori_skill reach 0.80 (Task 1) and 0.73 (Task 2); the baseline/definition behind 42 pp is not stated.

expectations.applies_when: A multi-objective framing is the headline contribution.
expectations.question: Is multi-objective selection ablated against pass-only selection?
expectations.reason: No single-objective arm; cost benefits are not separated from pruning enabled by any search.

claims.text: SkillMOO achieves the top pass-rate rank on 11 of 12 non-zero-pass tasks with lower cost than static bundles.
claims.setting: 16 SkillsBench SE tasks, GLM-5, 10 runs per method.
claims.baseline_control: ori_skill and no_skill; no equal-budget search baseline.
claims.selection_vs_test: Same task and same verifier used for fitness and reporting; fresh re-evaluation not stated.
claims.result_denominator: Mean +/- SD over 10 binary runs per task; Scott-Knott ESD ranks; 4 zero-pass tasks excluded from comparison but reported.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Per task, the search-selected bundle outperformed the original and empty bundles on the same verifier; the contribution of cost-aware selection or LLM edits versus any search is not isolated.

claims.text: Pruning and substitution are the dominant successful edit operations.
claims.selection_vs_test: Edits filtered from search traces with non-zero deltas.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Descriptive only (authors disclaim causality); Task 1 gains occurred with a single-skill bundle where pruning is impossible.
Plausible when the same task is repeated tens of times; one-shot tasks need a reliability argument.

claims.text: Treating skills as multi-objective objects is warranted over static or pass-only practice.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Motivated by static-bundle weakness (avg pass 0.14 vs 0.21 for no skill), but the benefit of the multi-objective part is not tested.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: For individual SkillsBench SE tasks, a small LLM-mutation + NSGA-II search over skill bundles found bundles with higher pass rate and often lower cost than the original or empty bundle on the same verifier suite (10 runs per task, GLM-5), at roughly $2-14 search cost per task.
not_supported: That multi-objective selection is needed (no pass-only/equal-budget arm).
Transfer of optimized bundles across tasks or models.
Causal role of pruning/substitution (authors say exploratory).
assessment.reproduction_note: Author-reported; not reproduced. Capped at task because selection and reporting share task and verifier.

G.reason: Concrete, sourced bottleneck (skills raise cost or mislead; external benchmarks plus the paper own Table 2 show original bundles averaging lower pass than no skill) with named closest neighbors (EvoSkill, EvoSkills, Meta Context Engineering, GEPA, ACE, Meta-Harness, LLM-guided GI) and a bounded delta (cost-aware Pareto selection). Neighbors are not run, so not 4.

M.reason: The bi-objective formulation directly answers the stated cost/misleading-guidance problem; mutation is grounded in evaluation evidence; edit types are enumerated and tied to the pruning-dominant observation. A distinguishing prediction against pass-only search is not tested, and the edit mechanism analysis is exploratory.

X.reason: Phases, population/generation sizes, objectives and selection are clear, but the optimizer prompts and edit application rules live outside the text, the final-bundle choice from the archive is unspecified, noise handling of single stochastic evaluations is absent, and there is no versioning, rollback or reuse protocol beyond a per-task archive.

E.measurement.reason: Objective execution-based verifier (original gates plus manually checked expanded tests), USD cost and runtime, plus the no_skill majority-style baseline. Minor concerns: LLM-expanded tests, inconsistent statements about which model generated them, and an abstract effect size that does not match Table 2.

E.causality.reason: Comparisons are against the static original and empty bundles only. No pass-only, random-edit/subset or budget-matched search arm; multi-objective benefit, LLM edits and population search are not separated; Task 1 gains occur with a single-skill bundle where only content edits are possible, indicating verifier-specific rewriting; authors defer causal edit studies.

E.holdout.reason: Search and reporting use the same task and the same verifier suite, with no held-out tasks or models and an unstated fresh re-evaluation; scope limited to one benchmark and one LLM. The authors disclose these limits and list transfer as future work.

E.statistics.reason: 10 independent runs per method per task, mean +/- SD, Scott-Knott ESD ranks, hypervolume, and explicit reporting of zero-pass tasks excluded from comparison. Limits: binary outcomes with n=10 give wide intervals and no multiple-comparison treatment.

E.cost.reason: Per-task search cost, runtime, hypervolume per dollar and a cost-only break-even reuse analysis are reported, with per-candidate cost ranges and timeouts. Baselines do not receive the same evaluation budget, and cost is dollar-only (GLM-5 pricing).

reason: Full HTML text read; all items resolved; prompts and replication package are external.
rationale: 问题定位清晰、统计与成本报告较规范，但缺少预算对齐/仅通过率搜索对照，选择与报告共用同一任务与验证器；多目标收益与编辑机制未被隔离。
